title: Microcost Forensics — per-token latency & cost wires (session notes)
content:
Summary:
Quick notes from the 2025-11-06 cross-team wireframe session: we sketched a focused investigation view to let engineers and platform owners 'forensically' examine per-invocation token cost and latency contributors. The goal is a compact, query-first panel that surfaces suspect invocations, token spans (prompt vs. generated), model/variant routing, batching/caching impact, and potential fallback events.

Why a new view?
- Existing console pages give aggregate token cost and per-route cost breakdowns, but it's hard to trace an expensive tail to specific token slices or rollout decisions.
- Customers repeatedly ask: "Which tokens in my convo are driving cost spikes? Is the model variant or context length the culprit?"
- We want a tool that supports incident triage, cost regression debugging, and post-rollout QA.

Primary goals (product hypotheses):
1) Reduce time-to-root-cause for high-cost invocations from hours to <15 minutes for SRE/product teams.
2) Provide actionable fixes: suggest batching/quantization/route tweaks based on observed patterns.
3) Make token-level traces queryable and linkable (so support + shareable investigation links).

Primary personas:
- Eng-SRE: triage spikes and enforce SLOs
- Platform/ML infra: optimize batching & model placement policies
- Product engineers: verify rollout impact on unit economics

Key metrics to show on the panel (minimum viable):
- Invocation list (sortable): time, route, model-variant, total tokens, total cost (USD), p50/p95 latency
- Token span breakdown for a selected invocation: prompt tokens, prompt cost, gen tokens, gen cost, kv-cache hits
- Per-token timeline heatmap: token index vs. latency/contrib to cost (hot tokens colored)
- Routing & fallback timeline: where requests routed, fallbacks to smaller models, region swaps
- Batch context: whether request was batched and its batch size, estimated batching savings

Wireframe sketches (text sketches from whiteboard):
[Top bar] Query bar: time window + route filter + min-cost threshold + search by invocation-id
[Left column] Invocation list (compact rows):
  - Row: timestamp | route | variant | tokens | cost | p95 | quick-tags (fallback/batched/kv-hit)
[Center pane] Invocation detail (selected row):
  - Header: invocation-id, share-link, raw request+response snapshot (collapsed)
  - Row: token-span summary (horizontal bars) -> prompt | preprompt | gen | special tokens
  - Heatmap: 1..N tokens on X, metric (latency or cost) on Y (log-scaled colors)
  - Timeline: sequence of server events (queued -> scheduled -> kernel-> completed); hover shows durations
[Right column] Suggested remediations and facts:
  - Suggested: reduce max_tokens, consider quantized-variant (X% unit cost reduction), enable prefix cache for route Y
  - Recent rollouts touching this route (canary id, start time)

Notes on interactions:
- Selecting a token in the heatmap highlights the corresponding text in the request/response snapshot.
- Invocation rows should show an expandable stacktrace-like trace of model calls when multi-model routing occurred.
- Share link should capture current filters + selected invocation as a short id (for Pager/Slack).
- Allow pinning token-slices as 'evidence' to a case (for CS handoffs).

Edge cases & UX tradeoffs: 
- Volume: customers with millions of invocations - need server-side paging and sampling. Plan: default to p95+ cost tail sampling, allow 'show all' for narrow filters.
- Privacy: raw request snapshots may contain PII; default collapse and require ACL to unmask. Flag: redact by default, require 'view-raw' perm.
- Storage/Retention: token-level traces are heavy. Default retention 7 days for all customers, 90 days for enterprise with add-on. UI must show retention window and offer 'export' for long-term archive.
- Performance: generating heatmaps for huge tokens length is expensive. Implement downsampling and log color scaling.

Backlog grooming (ordered):
1) MFE scaffolding + invocation list stub (JIRA-UI-902) - minimal columns, server-side paging, link to existing cost API. (Owner: Benji)
  - AC: list renders, filters time window, pages.
2) Invocation detail panel + raw snapshot expand (JIRA-UI-908) - include share-link, redact toggle, permission check. (Owner: Sofia)
  - AC: click row opens panel, snapshot shows truncated request, share-link copies a stable URL.
3) Token-span rendering + heatmap (JIRA-ML-914) - backend endpoint for token metrics + downsampling logic. (Owner: Lars)
  - AC: selecting invocation fetches token series; heatmap displayed; hover shows token index and metric.
4) Routing & fallback timeline visualization (JIRA-DEV-927) - attach routing events from audit logs. (Owner: Maya)
  - AC: timeline shows events; when hovered shows event metadata (region, variant).
5) Suggestions engine (JIRA-UX-945) - simple rules initially (if gen_tokens>prompt_tokens by X and cost>Y -> recommend variant). (Owner: Aisha)
  - AC: for sample cases produces at least one suggestion with estimated savings.
6) Shareable investigation links + pinning (JIRA-SRE-950) - persist selected invocation snapshot & filters for 30 days.
  - AC: link resolves to the same view for users with access.
7) Export & retention settings in settings panel (JIRA-OPS-961)
  - AC: admins can set retention and trigger exports.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Investigations must surface the top contributing token spans and allow engineers to create an action (tkt, suggestion) from the UI in <3 clicks.
- UI must maintain <200ms interaction latency for typical pages (<=100 rows), degrade gracefully for larger data sets with 'sampling applied' badge.
- Suggested remediations should include a conservative estimate of cost/latency impact and link to runbook.

Open questions (need decisions):
- How granular should the heatmap be for very long sequences (>2048 tokens)? Downsample or chunk pages? (Tradeoff: fidelity vs. compute).
- Do we show estimated dollar cost per token or per-span only? Customers like per-token $ for explainability, but it implies per-token price math in UI.
- Where does this surface live in nav? A new top-level 'Forensics' entry or a modal from the existing route cost page? Recommendation: add 'Investigations' as a subtab under Console -> Observability so it is discoverable by SREs.
- Permission model: should 'view-raw' be part of existing admin roles or a new granular permission?

Design notes / micro-interactions to capture for handoff:
- Heatmap tooltip should include: token text (truncated), token index, lat-ms, cost-USD, upstream event id.
- Quick-filters: show only invocations with fallbacks OR p95>X OR cost>Y. These filters should be composable and preserved in share-link.
- Visual language: use teal for cached/kv-hit positive, amber for long-latency tokens, red for high per-token-cost; consistent with existing console palette.
- Empty state: if no invocations found, show short playbook: "How to surface suspects" with a link to runbooks and an example Jupyter notebook to extract local traces.

Prototype tasks (short-term):
- Benji: wire up MFE scaffold and fake data table (1 week)
- Lars: prototype API response shape for token series + downsampling strategy (1 week)
- Sofia: create low-fidelity Figma with the three-column layout and heatmap interactions (3 days)
- Aisha: write initial suggestions rules and runbook links (3 days)

Notes to self / backlog scribbles:
- Consider quick 'what-if' toggle: show estimated savings if route switched to quantized-variant — compute via simple multiplier using model profile.
- Could reuse existing token inspector components but need to side-step performance bottlenecks. Investigate reusing microtoken-inspector's rendering layer (PR 331) but with server-side sampling.
- Follow up with Legal on PII retention policy before enabling raw snapshot exports (OWN: legal@redwood).

Meeting decisions (11/06):
- Build as a subtab under Observability (agreed)
- Default retention: 7 days, enterprise opt-in 90 days (agreed)
- Redaction-by-default for raw snapshots (agreed)

Next steps (owner list):
- Aisha: finalize acceptance criteria and update Confluence page (due 2025-11-10)
- Benji: create JIRA-UI-902 and add initial mock server (due 2025-11-13)
- Sofia: Figma screens for review on 2025-11-09
- Lars: prototype endpoint + perf report (due 2025-11-15)

Misc / Brainstorm fragments (keep as notes):
- 'Slice surgeon' metaphor: allow users to cut out a token span and see its computed contribution to downstream prompts (fun name, might be cute in internal docs only).
- Auto-detect 'anomalous spans' via a simple z-score on per-token latency over a sliding baseline; display an 'anomaly score' badge.
- Investigate cheaply computing token cost by mapping model-profile token-weight buckets rather than exact per-token compute.

Raw snapshot example (redacted):
---- BEGIN SNAPSHOT ----
invocation: abc123
route: svc/chat/v1
variant: gptx-q4-8k
user_id: <redacted>
tokens: 182 (prompt 98 / gen 84)
cost_usd: $0.024
latency_p95: 450ms
trace: queued(12ms) -> scheduled(20ms) -> kernel(360ms) -> completed(58ms)
---- END SNAPSHOT ----

If you want to iterate on language for the suggested remedies, I can prepare 3 phrasing variants (concise / technical / exec-friendly) to A/B across customer reactions.

-- Aisha
